items.performers: Gidon Kremer (violin), Boston Symphony Orchestra, Charles Dutoit (conductor)
items.label: Deutsche Grammophon 427 336-2
items.note: This violin concerto takes Bach’s royal theme apart, removing notes from each end before rebuilding it for a final backwards statement. Kremer, the dedicatee, plays with Dutoit and the Boston Symphony in the recording that earned Gubaidulina the 1989 Koussevitzky International Recording Award.

items.performers: Boris Pergamenschikow (cello), Elsbeth Moser (bayan), Münchener Kammerorchester, Christoph Poppen (conductor)
items.label: ECM New Series 1775
items.note: Cello, bayan — the Russian button accordion — and strings meditate on Christ’s last sayings from the Cross. Moser and Pergamenschikow make the two solo instruments merge, against the Munich Chamber Orchestra’s clear strings.

items.performers: Anne-Sophie Mutter (violin), London Symphony Orchestra, Valery Gergiev (conductor)
items.recorded: February 2008, AIR Studios, Lyndhurst Hall, London
items.label: Deutsche Grammophon 477 7450
items.note: The solo violin faces an orchestra with no violins of its own: fifteen violas, twelve cellos and nine double basses form the string section. Mutter, the concerto’s dedicatee and first soloist, makes its first recording with Gergiev and the London Symphony Orchestra.
